title: Disaggregated Multi-Tower: Topology-aware Modeling Technique for Efficient Large Scale Recommendation
problem: Large-scale recommendation systems using multi-tower architectures face efficiency challenges when deployed across heterogeneous hardware topologies. Traditional tower designs do not account for hardware topology constraints, resulting in suboptimal resource utilization and excessive communication overhead.
motivation: Recommendation systems are critical production workloads at internet scale, and topology-aware optimization is essential to minimize latency and energy consumption while scaling to billions of interactions.
method: The system breaks a recommendation model into many small pieces and assigns each piece to run on a specific processor, using an algorithm that considers the hardware topology (how computers are physically connected), network bandwidth, communication latency, and compute capabilities. It then schedules the work so that pieces that exchange data run close together, which reduces how much data needs to travel between different parts of the hardware.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using hardware topology information (how processors are connected and how fast they can communicate) to guide where each piece of the recommendation model gets placed, which reduces unnecessary data moving between machines.
contributions: Topology-aware disaggregation framework for multi-tower recommendation architectures
Hardware-aware component placement and scheduling strategy
Demonstration of efficiency improvements in large-scale recommendation deployment
